issue.title: Resume pending stitch hook-failure steps on commit-finalizer retry
issue.description: Commit-finalizer retry currently treats a plain stitch_failed after-commit hook failure as a retryable finalizer failure, but the retry path starts a new stitch attempt instead of resuming the checkpoint left in commit_state.json. The conflict-repair path invokes run_stitch_resume for EXIT_CODE_CONFLICT; hook failures that occur after the commit lands leave completed_steps such as dispatch/file_hooks recorded and require manual 'sase stitch create --resume'.

task_type_fields.proposal: When builtin@commit retries after a plain stitch_failed result, detect a run-owned pending commit_state.json checkpoint for that repo and resume the pending stitch steps before starting a new stitch create. Preserve the existing conflict-repair resume path and fail closed if the checkpoint does not match the current run/repo.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: This was discovered while fixing the retry-loop and already-clean proof bug from plan 202609/fix_commit_finalizer_retry_loop.md. The approved fix only guarantees the finalizer terminates and accepts a repo already committed by an earlier attempt of the same run; automatically completing the pending after-commit hook workflow is a separate behavior change.

payload.description: Adjacent resume behavior in sase stitch create --resume: sase-po hardens resume identity checks, while this task teaches builtin@commit retry to resume pending hook-failed stitch steps.
